files.lesson.md: --- order: 25 unit: enlarge9 node: AC9M9SP02 n1 uses: [AC9M8SP01 n1] assumes: [AC9M8SP01 n1] connection: screen-ratio title: What enlargement keeps summary: "An enlargement multiplies every length by the same scale factor. It keeps the angles and the shape, and changes the lengths, the perimeter and the area." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A video made for a TV screen is shown on a phone. Why does it sometimes have black bars?" --- A video is 1920 pixels wide and 1080 tall. A phone screen is 2400 by 1080. Can you enlarge or shrink the video so it fills the phone exactly? Have a guess, and we'll come back to it at the end. (These screen sizes are examples: your own phone's settings will show its size.) ## Predict: what stays the same ```step stage: predict insight: "Choosing the angles of an enlarged triangle shows whether students think angles scale with the sides." check: type: predict q: "A triangle has angles 30°, 60° and 90°. It is enlarged with a scale factor of 2. What are the angles of the enlarged triangle?" options: - "30°, 60° and 90°" - "60°, 120° and 180°" - "15°, 30° and 45°" - "30°, 60° and 120°" actual: "30°, 60° and 90°. An enlargement keeps the angles; only the lengths change. Angles in a triangle must still add to 180°, which the doubled angles (360°) would not." ``` ## Run: enlarge it ```step stage: run insight: "Every length is multiplied by the scale factor, so a 6 cm side becomes 12 cm when the factor is 2." check: { type: number, q: "A shape has a 6 cm side. It is enlarged with a scale factor of 2. How long is the new side? (cm)", answer: 12, explain: "6 × 2 = 12 cm." } ``` ## Investigate: kept and changed ```step stage: investigate insight: "Angles and shape are kept. Lengths and the perimeter grow by the scale factor, and the area grows by more." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A rectangle is 4 cm by 3 cm. It is enlarged by a scale factor of 3. How long is the longer side now? (cm)" answer: 12 explain: "4 × 3 = 12 cm." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $4 \\times 3$?", answer: 12, explain: "4 × 3 = 12." } - check: type: question q: "Which of these does an enlargement keep?" options: ["Angles and the shape", "Side lengths", "Area", "Perimeter"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Every length is multiplied.", "Area changes too.", "The perimeter is a length, so it is multiplied."] explain: "The angles and the shape stay the same: only the size changes." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#kim" text: "Kim enlarges a triangle. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: enlarge-angles-grow explain: "Line 3: the angles stay at 40°, 60°, 80° because the shape is the same. If all three doubled they would add to 360°." ``` ### Kept and changed ```worked \text{angles: } 40°, 60°, 80° \to 40°, 60°, 80° :: Kept: the shape is the same. \text{sides: } 3, 4, 5 \to 6, 8, 10 :: Changed: every side is multiplied by 2. \text{perimeter: } 12 \to 24 :: Also multiplied by 2. \text{area: } 6 \to 24 :: Changed by more: 2 × 2 = 4 times bigger. ``` ### Keep and change ### Find the mistake Read Kim's working. Which line changes the angles? ## Modify: change the factor ```step stage: modify insight: "A factor between 0 and 1 shrinks the shape, and unequal stretching is not an enlargement." tasks: - hint: ["Multiply every length by 0.5.", "A scale factor under 1 shrinks a shape."] check: { type: number, q: "A side is $10$ cm. It is enlarged with a scale factor of $0.5$. How long is it now? (cm)", answer: 5, explain: "10 × 0.5 = 5 cm: a reduction is an enlargement with a factor below 1." } - hint: ["Divide the new length by the old.", "15 ÷ 6."] check: { type: number, q: "A side of $6$ cm becomes $15$ cm. What is the scale factor?", answer: 2.5, tolerance: 0.001, explain: "15 ÷ 6 = 2.5." } - hint: ["Does every length get the same factor?", "Compare 1920 ÷ 1080 with 2400 ÷ 1080."] check: { type: question, q: "A $1920$ by $1080$ picture is stretched to $2400$ by $1080$. Is that an enlargement?", options: ["No: the width grew by more than the height, so the shape changed", "Yes: it is bigger", "Yes: the height is the same", "Can't tell"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "Bigger isn't enough: every length needs the same factor.", "The width was multiplied by 1.25 and the height by 1.", "You can tell: the factors differ."], explain: "2400 ÷ 1920 = 1.25 but 1080 ÷ 1080 = 1. The factors aren't the same, so it's stretched, not enlarged." } ``` ### A smaller copy ### The factor ### Is it an enlargement ## Practise: keep and change ```step stage: practise insight: "Using the scale factor on lengths and remembering the angles stay." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A triangle has a 50° angle. It is enlarged by a scale factor of 4. What is that angle now? (degrees)" answer: 50 explain: "Angles are kept." - check: type: number q: "A rectangle is 5 cm by 2 cm. Enlarge it by a scale factor of 3. What is its perimeter? (cm)" answer: 42 explain: "The new sides are 15 and 6, so the perimeter is 2 × (15 + 6) = 42." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What are the new side lengths after multiplying 5 and 2 by 3? Give the longer one.", answer: 15, explain: "5 × 3 = 15, 2 × 3 = 6." } - check: type: number q: "Review: tan⁻¹ of 1 is what angle?" answer: 45 tolerance: 0.5 explain: "tan 45° = 1." ``` ### An angle ### The perimeter ### Review ## Make: fit the screen ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the screens: check whether a scale factor takes one screen shape to the other." tasks: - hint: ["Divide each length of the phone by the matching length of the video.", "Compare the two factors."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A video is 1920 by 1080. A phone screen is 2400 by 1080. Scale the video so its width is 2400. How tall is it? (Screen sizes are examples.)" steps: - ["$2400 \\div 1920 = 1.25$", "the scale factor for the width"] - ["$1080 \\times 1.25 = 1350$", "multiply the height by the same factor"] - ["1350 pixels, which is taller than 1080", "it doesn't fit"] answer: "1350" answerLabel: "Height (pixels)" tolerance: 0.5 feedback: - ["1080", "That is the original height. Multiply it by the same factor as the width."] - ["1.25", "That's the scale factor. Use it on the height."] criteria: - "I found one scale factor from the width." - "I used the same factor on the height." - "I compared with the screen's height." explain: "1080 × 1.25 = 1350, but the screen is only 1080 tall, so the video has to be smaller or cropped." - check: type: question q: "So how does a video fill a screen of a different shape?" options: ["It leaves bars or crops, because one scale factor can't fit both lengths", "It changes the angles", "It uses a different scale factor for each side", "It always fits"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Angles stay the same in an enlargement.", "Different factors would stretch the picture.", "Only the same shape fits exactly."] explain: "An enlargement keeps the shape, so a different-shaped screen leaves bars or crops the picture (or stretches it)." ``` ### The height ### What the screen does **Also used in** - **Photos and posters.** Enlarging a photo keeps the shape; cropping changes it. - **Maps.** Every length on a map is scaled by the same factor. - **Next lesson.** What happens to area and volume. ```teacher summary: Students say what an enlargement keeps (angles, shape) and what it changes (lengths, perimeter, area) (AC9M9SP02, node 1). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 6 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 11 min goals: - I can say what stays the same in an enlargement. - I can use a scale factor to find a length. - I can tell an enlargement from a stretch. struggle: "Thinking angles scale. Ask: do the angles in a triangle still have to add to 180°?" before: > Students need Similar shapes (Year 8). The one idea: one scale factor for every length, and the angles stay. A factor under 1 is a reduction. The screen sizes are examples; students can check their own device. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check." - "Paper: the screen question in Make is worked on paper first." stuck: - see: A student says the angles double. ask: Do the angles in a triangle still add to 180°? fix: Doubled angles would add to 360°, so they can't change. stretch: Find a screen size for which 1920 by 1080 fits exactly. support: A printed grid with a shape and its enlargement. leads: | Continues AC9M9SP02 node 1. Where it leads: Scale factors for area and volume. exit: q: A shape is enlarged by a scale factor of 3. What happens to the angles? a: They stay the same. explain: > An enlargement multiplies every length by the same scale factor. The angles and the shape stay the same. A different factor for width and height is a stretch, not an enlargement. ```
